S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
examples: Makes mistakes in homework or tests by misreading questions or skipping important parts.
Frequently omits details or makes typos in work documents or reports.
Repeats mistakes in calculations or numerical work, such as switching signs or getting digits wrong.
Performs tasks incorrectly by missing important details in instructions.

S005.name: Organization_Difficulty
S005.description: Often has difficulty organizing tasks and activities.
examples: Desk, bag, or room is always messy and remains disorganized.
Unable to prioritize or determine the order of tasks, starting them randomly.
Fails to plan time effectively, frequently missing deadlines or rushing to finish at the last minute.
Feels overwhelmed by how to start multi-step projects and procrastinates.

S006.name: Sustained_Mental_Effort_Avoidance
S006.description: Often avoids, dislikes, or is reluctant to engage in tasks that require sustained mental effort.
examples: Continually procrastinates or is reluctant to start writing long reports or complex homework.
Avoids activities that require long periods of concentration, such as reading books or studying.
Passes off tasks that require complex thinking or planning to others.
Gets annoyed or resists when asked to start a task that requires significant mental effort.

S008.name: Distractibility
S008.description: Often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).
examples: Easily distracted and stops working due to small noises or movements nearby.
Cannot concentrate because eyes keep wandering to the scenery outside the window or people passing by.
Starts daydreaming or gets sidetracked by sudden thoughts while working or studying.
Loses focus and listens in when hearing side conversations or TV sounds.

S009.name: Daily_Activities_Forgetfulness
S009.description: Often forgetful in daily activities (e.g., doing chores, running errands; for older adolescents and adults, returning calls, paying bills, keeping appointments).
examples: Forgets appointment times or meeting schedules, arriving late or missing them entirely.
Forgets to reply to received calls or messages for days.
Frequently incurs late fees because of missing deadlines for utility bills or credit card payments.
Forgets to take medication or leaves necessary items at home when going out.

S015.name: Excessive_Talking
examples: Talks incessantly and cannot tolerate silence, continuing to chatter.
Continues to talk even when others are bored or try to cut the conversation short.
Talks too much inappropriately for the situation, making people around them uncomfortable.
Monopolizes the conversation and gives almost no chance for others to speak.

patient_info.stressor_event: Major change in responsibilities at work (e.g., promotion, demotion)
patient_info.stressor: Robin’s difficulties became clinically significant after she was given expanded charge-nurse responsibilities on the medical-surgical floor, including coordinating patient flow, mentoring newer nurses, and auditing EHR documentation across shifts. During the following 1 year and 11 months, the higher cognitive load overwhelmed the rigid routines she had relied on, and recurring detail errors, trouble organizing competing tasks, reluctance to start documentation-heavy reviews, distractibility in a noisy unit, forgotten follow-ups, and excessive talking during handoffs began interfering with patient-care workflow. The impairment became severe because her performance concerns escalated to formal supervision, coworkers had to double-check key administrative tasks, and her off-duty life also became strained by missed appointments and neglected household obligations. She entered psychiatric care through an employee assistance program after occupational health recommended evaluation as part of a work-performance remediation plan.

S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
S001.manifestation: I’ll think I’ve finished an EHR audit or checked a transfer note, and then my supervisor finds that I missed a required field, put the wrong time on a medication follow-up, or copied the wrong room number even though I swear I looked right at it.

S005.name: Organization_Difficulty
S005.description: Often has difficulty organizing tasks and activities.
S005.manifestation: When I’m charge nurse, I have scraps of paper, sticky notes, and half-started lists everywhere, but I still can’t seem to decide what has to happen first, so I end up putting out whatever fire is loudest and then rushing at the end of the shift.

S006.name: Sustained_Mental_Effort_Avoidance
S006.description: Often avoids, dislikes, or is reluctant to engage in tasks that require sustained mental effort.
S006.manifestation: If I know a task is going to take a lot of focused chart review, like auditing documentation across shifts, I keep pushing it off and finding bedside tasks to do instead because sitting down with it feels like trying to climb a wall.

S008.name: Distractibility
S008.description: Often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).
S008.manifestation: The main reason I’m here is that on the floor I lose my train of thought constantly—an IV pump beeps, someone asks another nurse a question, or a call light goes off, and suddenly I’ve forgotten what patient flow issue I was working on.

S009.name: Daily_Activities_Forgetfulness
S009.description: Often forgetful in daily activities (e.g., doing chores, running errands; for older adolescents and adults, returning calls, paying bills, keeping appointments).
S009.manifestation: I forget things that should be routine, like calling a family member back, following up on a missing order, paying a bill at home, or showing up for an appointment, even when I meant to do it and sometimes even after I set a reminder.

S015.name: Excessive_Talking
S015.manifestation: During handoff or when I’m mentoring a newer nurse, I catch myself giving way too much background and talking in circles until people are glancing at the clock or trying to jump in, and I still have trouble wrapping it up.

additional_requirement_1.name: Additional Requirement 1
additional_requirement_1.manifestation: Even in elementary school, my teachers wrote that I was bright but careless and always losing worksheets or forgetting to turn in homework, and my mom had to sit with me every night to keep me on track.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: At work, the concerns have gotten serious enough that I’m on formal supervision and other nurses have to double-check parts of my charge-nurse follow-through, which makes me feel like I’m becoming a liability instead of a leader.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been a major problem since I took on the expanded charge-nurse responsibilities almost two years ago.
